description: RC materials/discretization — material layer mapping, RC network construction, and window models

reviews.title: HPXML construction material layers to RC network node mapping correctness
reviews.prompt: Trace how HPXML material layers map to RC capacitances and resistances. Diurnal penetration depth criterion correctly applied per ISO 13786:2007? Insulation modeled as single-node? Material property IP-to-SI conversion correct? Window layers follow E+ 5-step? The mapping from HPXML construction layers (defined as a sequence of Material elements with thickness, conductivity, density, specific heat) to the RC network nodes must be traced end-to-end. The diurnal penetration depth criterion from ISO 13786:2007 determines whether a material layer is thermally 'thick' (needs multiple RC nodes to resolve transient behavior) or 'thin' (can be lumped into adjacent nodes) — verify that this criterion uses the correct angular frequency (2π / 86400) and that the threshold for lumping is correctly applied. Pure insulation layers (very low conductivity, negligible heat capacity) should be modeled as a single thermal resistance with zero capacitance, not broken into unnecessary nodes. All material property conversions from IP units (inch, BTU, lb/ft³, BTU/lb·°F) to SI (m, W/m·K, kg/m³, J/kg·K) must use exact conversion factors: verify 1 inch = 0.0254 m, 1 BTU/h·ft·°F = 1.730735 W/m·K, 1 lb/ft³ = 16.0185 kg/m³, 1 BTU/lb·°F = 4186.8 J/kg·K. Window construction layers must follow EnergyPlus's 5-step glazing model: (1) compute overall U-factor from center-of-glass plus frame edge effects, (2) compute SHGC with angular dependence, (3) split SHGC into transmitted and absorbed portions, (4) distribute absorbed solar by layer, and (5) model convective/radiative heat transfer at each glass surface.

reviews.title: RC network discretization: node count, time constants, stability
reviews.prompt: split_layer_count() correct for all material types? Time constants physically plausible (no sub-second)? System observable (all thermal mass affects zone air)? Same-zone boundary inner-half-layer handling correct? The split_layer_count() function determines how many RC nodes to create for each material layer based on its diurnal penetration depth. Verify that it produces at least one node per layer, that the number of nodes does not exceed a practical limit (e.g., 20 nodes for even the thickest concrete wall), and that the split is deterministic for the same material properties. Compute the smallest RC time constant (R * C for each node pair) and verify it does not fall below the simulation timestep — sub-second time constants indicate numerical stiffness that may require implicit solution methods or timestep reduction. The state-space system derived from the RC network must be observable: every thermal capacitance (C-node) must be connected to the zone air node through some path of conductances, otherwise it represents isolated thermal mass that the solver tracks but that never affects zone air temperature. For same-zone boundary surfaces (interior walls between two rooms in the same thermal zone), the 'inner half layer' of the construction must be modeled as exposed to zone air on both sides rather than splitting the construction asymmetrically — verify that this symmetry is enforced and that the thermal mass of the construction is correctly attributed to the zone.

reviews.title: Window material model: IAM curves, SHGC decomposition, U-factor three-resistance split
reviews.prompt: 6 IAM polynomial curves correct per glazing type? SHGC decomposed into transmitted+absorbed per E+ steps 1-5? Three-resistance decomposition (r_glass, r_film_interior, r_film_exterior) physically correct? Walton effective-temperature correction for exterior LWR correct? Verify that the six standard incident angle modifier (IAM) polynomial curve types — uncoated single, uncoated double, uncoated triple, low-e single, low-e double, low-e triple — are implemented with the correct polynomial coefficients as defined in the ASHRAE Handbook or EnergyPlus engineering reference. The SHGC decomposition must split the total solar heat gain into directly transmitted solar radiation (absorbed by interior surfaces) and absorbed solar radiation per glass layer (re-radiated as longwave to interior) following EnergyPlus steps 1-5 exactly. The three-resistance U-factor model splits the window's overall thermal resistance into three components in series: exterior air film resistance (r_film_exterior), glass panel conductance (r_glass computed from center-of-glass U-factor minus film resistances), and interior air film resistance (r_film_interior). Verify that r_film_exterior uses the correct wind-speed-dependent correlation and that r_film_interior uses the correct natural convection correlation. The Walton effective-temperature correction for exterior longwave radiation exchange — which accounts for the fact that exterior surfaces see sky, ground, and surrounding objects at different temperatures — must be applied to the exterior longwave boundary condition at each window surface; verify the effective sky temperature formula T_sky = T_db * (0.787 + 0.0028 * (T_dew - 273.15) + 0.0024 * opaque_sky_cover) matches the EnergyPlus implementation.
